subject: R - Chi Square Difference Test, set correlation to 1

messages.author: 96faf9bf86572bf8
messages.subject: R - Chi Square Difference Test, set correlation to 1
parts:
Hey there, 

I'm working on my master thesis and I'm not sure how to interpret an error message by R. I have 5 latent Variables (DI, PR, BQ, RA and RV). Since the Fornell Larcker Kriterium is in some cases not met, I'd like to do an Chi Squared Difference Test, thus setting the correlation to one and compare the Chi Squared-Values of the two models: My model with the fixed correlation is this one:

Modell <-'DI =~ NA*DI_3 + DI_1 + DI_4 + DI_5 + DI_6
PR =~ NA*PR_2 + PR_1 + PR_3
BQ =~ ZUF_2 + VER_1
RA =~ ABS_1 + ABS_2 + ABS_4
RV =~ NWOM_2 + MA_1 + RB_2
DI ~~ 1*DI
PR ~~ 1*PR
DI ~~ 1*PR'
fit <- cfa(Modell, data=Daten, estimator="mlr")
summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

Unfortunately I get an error message, but am still able to run the cfa. " covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate" Is this just due to the fact that I set the correlation between DI and PR to one?

Thank you so much !!!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: R - Chi Square Difference Test, set correlation to 1
parts: Unfortunately I get an error message, but am still able to run the cfa. " covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate" Is this just due to the fact that I set the correlation between DI and PR to one?

That sounds like you got a warning message, not an error message.  Yes, a correlation of 1 means that the matrix will have linear dependency because that would mean one variable is a linear transformation of the other.  Because you are doing that on purpose to test a hypothesis, you can ignore the warning.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
